summary: Baseline tests passed, but 13 of 143 maintenance tests failed because the implementation mishandles shared entries, symlink safety, raw index keys, and absent-index fail reporting.

details.reasoning: The production implementation is present and runs, but it misses several explicit integrity requirements. repair() adds every broken or resolved entry to its discard set before considering shared status, then removes those entries even when they are shared; this explains the shared-name, shared-link, hard-link, and shared-broken failures. Index and entry validation uses Files.isRegularFile(path) while following links, so links used as the index or links to files outside the folder are accepted instead of rejected or classified as broken. Known dangling-link entries are written through during save, creating their targets. The repair removal path also normalizes descriptions instead of removing the exact raw index key, breaking descriptions that differ only by CRLF versus LF. Finally, fail initialization rejects an absent index immediately and omits the unowned-file detail required by the corresponding fail report. These are all directly stated in the task and are not caused by test infrastructure.
details.secondary_factors: The agent also modified the existing reads_empty_list_of_violations test, replacing its original empty-list assertion with an absent-entry assertion. The baseline result is therefore not an untouched-baseline signal; reverting that edit would expose a compatibility mismatch in the agent's default save behavior. The trajectory also shows repeated Gradle compile retries and an offline Spotless failure, but the agent recovered and these did not block the final verifier run.

justification.issue_description: Shared entries are not preserved during repair, and path/link identity is not validated according to the store-integrity rules. Related failures include unsafe known-entry saves, CRLF/LF index-key removal, and incomplete fail reporting for an absent index.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly says entries recording the same name or reaching one file are shared, that an entry both shared and something else stays shared, that the index must be a regular file directly in the folder, that entries reaching outside through links are broken, and that unsafe saves must leave the store unchanged. In agent_solution.patch, repair() unconditionally collects broken/resolved descriptions before its shared check; isRegularFileDirectlyInFolder() calls Files.isRegularFile(path) without NOFOLLOW_LINKS; prepareStoredRulesFile() uses the same following-link validation; forgetRule() validates before it can safely remove only one member of a shared unsafe entry; and FileSyncedProperties.remove() normalizes the key. JUnit reports 13 assertion failures and zero errors, while the reference solution provides separate link-aware integrity classification and exact-key application.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because the missed behaviors are explicit, foreseeable filesystem-integrity cases in the task, not undocumented test conventions. The code follows a plausible overall design and passes 130 maintenance tests, but the omitted conditions change repair safety and data preservation, so this is not merely a formatting or verifier-expectation mismatch.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is demanding but fair: it specifies the naming, link identity, sharing, repair, fail-report, save-safety, and concurrency semantics in detail, and the reference implementation demonstrates that the behavior is solvable. The failing tests correspond to those stated semantics rather than hidden implementation details.

evidence: The wrapper completed normally with baseline_passed=true (42/42) and new_tests_passed=false (130/143); JUnit records 13 failures and 0 errors, not a bootstrap crash.
The failures are concrete assertion mismatches in FreezeStoreMaintenance_e448f3_Test, including entries being removed, symlinked indexes being accepted, and a missing notes.txt report entry.

The trajectory shows repeated compile polling/retries and an offline Spotless dependency issue, but the agent recovered, ran its own suite successfully, and delivered a production patch; no external failure persisted into grading.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker explains the failures; the dominant issue is incorrect production logic, with an additional concern that an existing baseline test was edited.
